subject: Post-demo security follow-up & subprocessor inventory

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo security follow-up & subprocessor inventory
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-list-v1.xlsx

Hi Emma — great to meet you and the NimbusCare team on the demo today. Quick recap and next steps from our side around the security/discovery items you raised: 

1) SOC 2: You asked whether Redwood has a current SOC 2 report covering our production inference service. Short answer: yes — we have a SOC 2 Type II report (2027) that covers our hosted inference platform and data handling controls. I attached a short summary (SOC2-quick-summary-2027.pdf) to save time; we can redact any business-sensitive sections for sharing with procurement.

2) Subprocessors / third-party roster: I attached our working subprocessor inventory (redwood-subprocessor-list-v1.xlsx). Top-level callouts: AWS (us-east-1) for compute & storage, Google Cloud BigQuery for analytics pipelines, Stripe for billing, and S3-compatible object stores via partners. We noted your question about geographic boundaries and whether tokenized data leaves the US — short answer is: for hosted customers in the US we keep inference workload and persistent storage within US regions by default; we can provide an architecture/data flow diagram if that helps.

3) Questionnaire: You mentioned a short vendor security questionnaire. If you can share the doc, we’ll kick off completion and assign a security point-of-contact. If you prefer, we can initiate our standard security questionnaire and send you a hosted link.

Proposed immediate next steps (feel free to adjust):
- Emma: share the vendor questionnaire or confirm preference for our hosted questionnaire link (by 8/4)
- Jordan/Ben: share the subprocessor list + SOC2 summary (done) and confirm region residency settings for a POC
- Marissa/Ben: prepare a brief architecture diagram showing data ingress → inference → storage with region annotations (deliver by 8/5)

If helpful, I can loop in Monica from our security team to own the questionnaire response and provide evidence items.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2: Great to hear you have a Type II report. Procurement will need either the full attestation or an executed NDA + redaction process. Can you confirm whether any subservices (e.g., third-party model hosting partners) are in scope of that SOC 2?

- Data residency: Our legal team requires confirmation that PHI will remain within US boundaries for the POC and that we can request an account-level setting for region restriction. Can you confirm the configuration option and whether anything (logs, analytics) might be replicated to non-US regions?

- Questionnaire: Attaching a 6-page security questionnaire (attached by separate email from procurement). If Redwood can initiate/own the questionnaire response, that would speed things up. We also need an initial subprocessor inventory with data categories mapped (e.g., 'Model inference tokens: processed; Storage: customer logs/analytics: pseudonymized metadata').

Ideally we’d like to have initial answers and the subprocessor mapping by end of next week, ahead of our internal architecture review.

Emma Lopez
Senior Technical Program Manager — Security & Partnerships
NimbusCare

Monica — looping you in to own the questionnaire response and to confirm the subprocessor mapping Emma requested. Thread below for context. Procurement from NimbusCare will send a 6-page questionnaire (they asked us to initiate). 

Key asks from NimbusCare: 
- Confirm whether any subservices are in-scope for our SOC2 attestation (they want clarity on downstream model hosting and analytics partners)
- Provide an account-level configuration note: can we guarantee US-only region residency for the POC? Identify any telemetry or analytics that might be replicated outside the US and whether those items can be disabled.
- Produce a short mapping table that ties each subprocessor to the categories of data they touch (inference tokens, request metadata, logs, billing info). The attached spreadsheet is our working roster; please flag any entries that need redaction or vendor contact info updated.

Proposed internal owners: 
- SOC2 & attestation questions: Monica
- Region residency & infra config: Ben
- Subprocessor mapping & spreadsheet cleanup: Marissa

Emma has asked for initial answers by 8/9 so they can include the notes in their architecture review. Let me know if that timeline is realistic.

Thanks — Jordan

Thanks for the heads-up, Jordan and team — I’ll take point. Quick plan and status: 

1) SOC 2 scope: Our 2027 Type II attestation covers the hosted inference service and our control environment for third-party procurement. The SOC2 scope explicitly includes compute providers we manage (AWS us-east-1) and our encryption key management flows; it does not include customer-managed private deployments. I will confirm whether the analytics/BI pipeline (BigQuery) was in scope for the 2027 report and flag any vendors that were excluded. Attached is the SOC2 quick summary for NimbusCare to share with procurement; if they require the full report we can request an executed NDA and provide a redacted copy.

2) Region residency & POC config: Ben — can you confirm the exact account-level setting to lock workloads to us-east-1 and any logs that may be stored in secondary regions? My expectation: inference and persistent customer blobs remain in the selected region; aggregated anonymous telemetry may be processed in other regions for product monitoring unless disabled. We can turn off telemetry for the POC.

3) Subprocessor mapping: I reviewed the spreadsheet and added a 'data_category' column (in my local copy). Marissa, please reconcile vendor descriptions and add contact emails for the top five subprocessors. I’ll produce the initial mapping table tying each vendor to 'inference tokens', 'request metadata', 'logs', 'billing' and send to NimbusCare by COB 8/9.

4) Questionnaire: I’ll own the security questionnaire response. Jordan — please forward the procurement doc when it arrives (or point me at the shared Drive link). Estimated ETA for completed questionnaire (initial pass): 8/9 EOD. If procurement requests evidence artifacts beyond the SOC2 redaction (e.g., policy excerpts, config screenshots), I’ll flag those and propose an evidence collection plan.

Timeline looks feasible — we’ll escalate if anything needs legal review or if we need to involve engineering for detailed infra screenshots.
